inputs.proposal: Core needs no global setup: ecuio_init and ecuio_shutdown become optional no-ops, init always returns ECUIO_OK, and the bridge and QML drop the coreInitialized gate.
inputs.original_proposal: Core needs no global setup: ecuio_init and ecuio_shutdown become optional no-ops, init always returns ECUIO_OK, and the bridge and QML drop the coreInitialized gate.

concerns: Future transport plugins might rely on a non‑no‑op ecuio_init, breaking after this change.
Unconditional ecuio_shutdown may affect sessions if a future transport expects init/shutdown pairing.
Removing the coreInitialized property reduces visibility of core state, potentially confusing UI developers.
Documentation of the new lifecycle (init no‑ops, shutdown no‑ops) is currently absent, increasing risk of misuse.
questions: Can we confirm that all existing transports (mock, raw, obd2, etc.) truly ignore ecuio_init?
Will any future manufacturer protocols require global initialization that this change would break?
How will the updated lifecycle be documented for external developers to avoid accidental misuse?
auto_engineer.reasoning: The change removes a redundant initialization gate without violating any current domain rules, but introduces potential future risks and documentation gaps that warrant acknowledgement.
